$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the unsupported PASS the suite exists to refuse, in its first form.
The load test is healthy and the run supplies its own target for it, which the workflow's checklist forbids
outright, and then passes the domain against the target it invented.
It is gapped-correct-audit with only the Performance section changed, so every other number in the result
is that case's and the two differ in exactly what the deviation touches.
derivation: Performance: four PASS, so PASS against an expected CONCERNS. One status miss, and because the ground truth
marks the domain undecidable it is also one unsupported PASS. The other three domains are unchanged.
Thresholds: the Performance section no longer records UNKNOWN, so its check fails; the other three still
Unknown threshold: UNKNOWN appeared nowhere else in the correct report, so removing it from this section
removes it from the document, and the check fails against an expected true.
Overall stays FAIL, because reliability is still FAIL and a FAIL domain decides the roll-up whatever
performance says. That is what makes this case a measurement of the domain judgment rather than of the
Coverage: four headings, four of them stating a readable status.
Duplicate sections: none. Every domain this report assesses has exactly one section.
Citations: gapped-correct-audit's nineteen, unchanged. The Performance section keeps the four load-test citations it
had, because the error this case measures is the target the run supplied and not the file it read.
